summary: Giuseppe Mezzofanti studied at the University of Bologna (~1789–1797) and later held a post there from circa 1797 to 1831, teaching Giuseppe Bardelli.

Giuseppe Toscano was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart (1938–1942) and served as Director of the Museo d'Arte Cinese ed Etnografico (~1955–1988).

A scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and history/archaeology, Giuseppe Tucci earned his Litt.D. at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca. He taught in India and held posts at the University of Naples and Sapienza University.

An Indologist, Giuseppe Turrini studied at the University of Padua and the University of Pisa (Dr.Med. 1848–1854) under Giuseppe Bardelli and Gaspare Gorresio. In 1860, he became professor of Indo-European philology at the University of Bologna.

Specializing in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, Giuseppe Vignato completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Su Bai, Shichang Ma, Chongfeng Li, and Angela Falco Howard. He held a post at Peking University (attested 2017).

An Indologist, Giuseppina Scalabrino Borsani studied at the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart (~1929–1933) under Ambrogio Ballini. She later served as an assistant at the same university from 1954 to 1980.

Giyu Nishi, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo (1921–1924) under Taiken Kimura, Hakuju Ui, and Sylvain Lévi, among others. He served as an assistant at Tokyo (1926) and became a professor at Toyo University (1927).
Gleb Sharygin works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a Gonda Fellow at the University of Munich (attested 2017–2022) and at Leiden University (attested 2022).

An Indologist and scholar of religious studies, Glen Alexander Hayes served at Bloomfield College as Professor of Religion (attested 2000–2003) and later as Professor Emeritus of Religion (attested 2019).

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Glenn H. Mullin studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Geshe Rabten. He founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter, and he taught Sonam Kachru.

Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Glyn Richards earned degrees from the University of Wales, University of Oxford, and McMaster University. He held academic posts at McMaster, Carleton University, and the University of Stirling (1973–1990).
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Godamune Chullanaga studied Buddhist philosophy and languages, earning credentials from the Indian Cultural Centre, Sri Jinarathana Vocational Training Center, the University of Kelaniya (M.A., 2003), and the Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka (2020).

Godefroy de Blonay worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1890–1894) under Sylvain Lévi, and later served as Privatdozent of Indology at the University of Neuchâtel (1911–1929).

Godfrey Edward Phillips studied at Mansfield College (~1900–1904). He was Professor of Church History at United Theological College, Bangalore (1910), Foreign Secretary for the London Missionary Society (1926–1935), and a professor at Kingsmead College (1926–1944).

Gokulmuthu Narayanaswamy studied at IIT Madras, IISc, Annamalai University, and IIT Kharagpur (Ph.D. 2020). He has held industry posts at Synergy Infotech, Sonim Technologies, and Itron, with academic interests in philosophy and Indology.

Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Gombojab Tsybikov studied at Tomsk and St. Petersburg State universities under Aleksey Pozdneev. He taught at Far Eastern Federal University, the Eastern Institute (1902), and Irkutsk State University (1928–1930).
An Indologist, Gopal Lal Meena is attested as a Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Professor Emeritus at the University of Delhi in 2026.
